title: Normalized derived scalar/tensor identification
statement:
Let $W$ be a scheme with its small pro-etale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], and let $\varphi:A\to B$ be a map of commutative ring sheaves. Use module sheaves and their ordinary unbounded derived categories [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Let $E$ be ordinary scalar extension and $T$ its canonical K-flat left derived functor with its specified counit [lem-pur-sheaf-ring-derived-coefficient-adjunction]. Let $r$ be exact restriction and $C=r(B)$ [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars]. Let $a$ be any signed-total tensor presentation on flat-term K-flat representatives [def-sfb-proetale-tensor-model]. There is a unique natural isomorphism
$$h:rT\xrightarrow{\sim}(-\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}C[0])$$
with the following normalization. The ordinary comparison $c_P:r(E P)\cong P\otimes_A C[0]$ sends $b\otimes x$ to $x\otimes b$ degreewise. Write $Q_A,Q_B$ for localization and $\kappa_P:rT(Q_A P)\to Q_A(r E P)$ for restriction of the specified universal scalar-derived counit followed by the exact-restriction factorization. For every pair of flat-term K-flat complexes $P,Q$ and every quasi-isomorphism $q:Q\to C[0]$,
$$\kappa_P\circ h_{Q_A P}^{-1}\circ a.\mathrm{tensor}(1,Q_Aq)\circ a.\mathrm{representative}_{P,Q}=Q_A(c_P^{-1}\circ(1_P\otimes q)).$$
This is the predicate IsDerivedTensor in the attached Lean declaration. Resolving $C$ is required only after tensoring with K-flat $P$, so no flatness of $B$ is assumed. The attached module also retains the existing ordinary comparison, scalar mate, source/target identifications and their definitions unchanged; these are constructions rather than additional unresolved assertions.

proof.text: Flat-term K-flat resolutions and resolving-representative full faithfulness give full faithfulness of restriction of bifunctors. Restriction of unary functors is also fully faithful: inflate a transformation through the first projection and recover it on the diagonal. Descend the representative isomorphism with preimageIso. Its representative components are exactly those constructed above. Substitute these components in the normalization equation and cancel the comparison isomorphisms; functoriality of Q gives the prescribed right side. For uniqueness, use one flat K-flat resolution q of C[0]. The representative isomorphism and tensor(1,Qq) are invertible, as is the restricted scalar counit. Cancel them in the two normalization equations to identify inverse components on every representative. Faithful restriction identifies the inverse natural transformations and hence the isomorphisms.

lean.statement:
theorem derivedTensorIso_existsUnique
    {W : Scheme.{u}}
    {A B : Sheaf (Scheme.ProEt.topology W) CommRingCat.{u + 1}}
    (φ : A ⟶ B)
    (a : Scheme.ProEtaleTensorModel W A) :
    ∃! h : Scheme.proEtaleRingDerivedExtension φ ⋙ (restriction φ).mapDerivedCategory ≅
        (Functor.curryObj a.tensor).flip.obj
          (DerivedCategory.Q.obj (coefficientComplex φ)),
      IsDerivedTensor φ a h
